Our undergraduate and graduate student training has been particularly impactful because it involved a combination of classroom instruction, hands-on technical projects, and work with industry — often leading to journal publications and conference presentations. Many former PowerAmerica students are now employed by companies such as Wolfspeed, GeneSiC, ABB, X-FAB, and others. Our website features a searchable database of student profiles summarizing their research experience, skills, and career interests. The student profiles are a valuable tool for members seeking talent for internships or employees. Additionally, member meetings often include activities such as student speed dating with industry, poster sessions, informal networking opportunities, résumé coaching, student project presentations, and other enrichment exercises. At the end of BP5, PowerAmerica had 16 university members, each making contributions in their respective areas of expertise. By the end of BP6, university membership reached 23. University faculty have been funded to develop teaching modules and training tools, as well as acquire specialized lab equipment that introduce WBG concepts and facilitate their use in working circuits and systems. WBG training for working professionals is incredibly important to increasing their use. It supports and encourages practitioners who are experienced working with Si semiconductors to learn about the distinct characteristics and superior system benefits of SiC and GaN. Obtaining the best performance from SiC and GaN requires particular design and packaging considerations, and we’ve strived to convey those in several ways: our annual WBG Short Course; twice-yearly tutorials concurrent with our meetings; special sessions we’ve organized at large industry conferences (APEC, ECCE, ISCRM, WiPDA, PEDG, etc.); and tailored invited talks by our CTO at member facilities to train their staff. The table below summarizes some of the major metrics of PowerAmerica’s EWD activities. 8 FINAL CONCLUSIONS & RECOMMENDATIONS PowerAmerica is a member-driven consortium of industry, universities, and national labs, accelerating the commercialization of energy-efficient SiC and GaN power semiconductor chips and electronics. Our membership spans the WBG technology ecosystem, including the leading U.S. universities that train the workforce. The work we perform is a critical enabler of the “electrification of everything” and a vital weapon in the push for decarbonization and energy sustainability. PowerAmerica started operations in 2015, with funding from the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) and cost-share from North Carolina State University (NCSU) and other members. DOE and NCSU funding ended in April 2021, and PowerAmerica has been a member-supported private consortium since then. In 2016, PowerAmerica initiated and supported the world’s first SiC chip foundry — X-FAB Texas — which has not only halted the bleeding of domestic SiC chip fabrication overseas but also brought companies from Europe and Asia to fabricate in the U.S. More than eight U.S.-based fabless semiconductor companies are currently in production at X-FAB Texas. A key aspect of our work has been educating 410 full-time university students in applied SiC and GaN power technology, while simultaneously facilitating internships and other university-industry collaborations.
